title: Pope Leo XIV Draws 700,000 People to Paris Mass
summary:
How many people does it take to fill a huge square in Paris? Try 700,000. That's how many gathered at the Place de la Concorde to see Pope Leo XIV on Saturday. The Pope rode down the famous Champs-Élysées avenue in his open-topped popemobile, waving to crowds.

During the Mass, the Pope had a special message for young people. He called them "today's Church" and praised their "enthusiasm, energy and commitment." He told Catholics not to keep their faith to themselves, but to "let it overflow so that those you meet may be refreshed."

The Pope is on a four-day visit to France. On Friday, he met President Emmanuel Macron and joined 80,000 young people at a stadium. Macron didn't attend the Mass — France has strict rules about separating church and government. But his wife Brigitte and the prime minister were there.

Earlier Saturday, the Pope visited a center that helps refugees. He praised the group for inviting people "to see those who are invisible." The Pope also warned about the dangers of artificial intelligence. Big crowds are expected for the rest of his trip.
why_it_matters: The Pope's message that young people are "today's Church" shows kids that they are not just the future — they matter and can lead right now, in their families, schools, and communities.

background_read: Pope Leo XIV (the leader of the Catholic Church, which has more than a billion members around the world) visited France for four days.
Paris (the capital city of France) is home to the Place de la Concorde, a huge public square near the Champs-Élysées where big crowds gather.
Emmanuel Macron (the president of France) did not go to the Mass, because France has a long rule that keeps religion and government separate.

WHAT: The Pope led a huge Mass, met 80,000 young people, visited a refugee center, and warned about artificial intelligence
WHERE: Paris, France — at the Place de la Concorde, the Champs-Élysées, and a stadium
WHY: His four-day visit is meant to share his faith and encourage Catholic young people

perspectives.description: Catholics who came to see the Pope felt excited and encouraged, especially young people he praised for their energy.
Some people noted that President Macron stayed away from the Mass because France keeps church and government separate.
The Pope also warned about the dangers of artificial intelligence, reminding people that new technology needs to be watched carefully.
